sections.name: File setup
sections.title: File header
sections.what: Explains that the file serves both contact discovery and job discovery.

sections.name: ExaResult
sections.title: Search result shape
sections.what: The shape of one search hit: web address, title, optional date, author, text, highlights and score.
sections.why: Gives every caller one common result format.
sections.watch_out: Most fields are optional, so check before using them.

sections.name: ExaSearchOptions
sections.title: Search settings shape
sections.what: The settings a search can take: result count, domain filters, date filter, category, search style and what page text to return. It also sets the service address.
sections.watch_out: Category values must match the service's allowed list exactly.

sections.name: exaSearch
sections.title: Core search call
sections.what: Sends one search to Exa and returns the results, or throws an error with the service's message.
sections.why: Shared engine used by the two helpers below.
sections.watch_out: Page text is requested by default, which makes each call heavier.

sections.name: exaPeopleSearch
sections.title: Searching for people
sections.what: Searches LinkedIn profile pages for people with given titles at a company, optionally in a location.
sections.why: Finds people to contact at target companies.
sections.watch_out: Results depend on public profile pages, which may be out of date or belong to someone with a common name.

sections.name: exaJobSearch
sections.title: Searching for jobs
sections.what: Searches the web for job postings matching a query from the last 30 days, optionally limited to chosen job sites.
sections.watch_out: The 30-day window is fixed in code, not a user setting.

summary: Client for the Exa web search service, used to find people's LinkedIn profiles and recent job postings.
purpose: Helps the user discover contacts and job openings on the web.
why: The header says it serves both contact discovery and job discovery. The choice of neural search is not explained in the code.
how: 1. Checks that the key is present. 2. Sends a search request with the query, result count, domain and date filters, and a choice of what page text to return. 3. Throws an error with the service's message on failure. 4. Two helpers build specific queries for people and for jobs.
inputs: An Exa API key, a search query, optional domain, date and category filters, and a result count.
outputs: A list of search results, each with a web address, title and optional text excerpt, highlights and score.
risks: Default settings request page text for every result, which makes each call heavier. The people query joins titles with the plain word OR, which neural search may not treat as a true OR, so results may be loose.
debug: A missing key error points to the settings page. A status code in the error shows the service rejected the request. Empty results usually mean the domain filter or date window is too narrow.
